title: Refactoring between abstract classes and interfaces
answer: You can refactor an abstract class into an interface or an interface into an abstract class, but it is not a mechanical one-to-one conversion. Instance fields, constructors, protected state, and single-inheritance constraints belong naturally to classes; multiple contracts and capability composition belong naturally to interfaces. A conversion may therefore require moving state or behavior elsewhere and can change client inheritance choices.
